newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Controls sale proceeds to cut debt.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Controls sale proceeds to cut debt.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc said Tuesday it had completed the previously announced sale of its Plastic Container Division to Schmalbach-Lubeca AG and expects to use proceeds from the sale to reduce debt.
Johnson Controls said it sold the division for about $650 million, subject to certain adjustments.

It said it will use after-tax proceeds, estimated at $475-$525 million, to partially reduce debt incurred from its $1.35 billion acquisition of Prince, an automotive interiors supplier. The Prince deal was completed in October 1996.

Johnson Controls said its financial results for the quarter ending March 31 will reflect an after-tax gain on the sale of the Plastic Container Division. The gain will be classified as part of discontinued operations.

The company said it expects to file reclassified financial statements with the Securities and Exchange Commission within the next 10 days reflecting the division as a discontinued operation. The division makes polyethylene terephthalate beverage and food bottles in North America, Europe and South America.
Johnson Controls makes and markets automotive systems and building controls.
